title: Loaded cost per pair: brackets matter
objective: Build a multi-step formula where brackets and the order of operations decide the answer.
instructions: Each line shows the number of pairs ordered, the unit cost, the freight for the whole order and an example duty rate (0.25 means 25%). In F2:F5, work out the loaded cost per pair: the unit cost plus duty on the unit cost, plus the freight per pair (whole-order freight divided by the number of pairs). In G2:G5, work out the freight per pair as a share of the loaded cost per pair (a decimal, so 0.1 means 10%). Use brackets where they are needed.
hints: Unit cost plus duty is C2*(1+E2). The brackets make Excel add 1 and the rate before multiplying.
Freight per pair is D2/B2, so the loaded cost is =C2*(1+E2)+D2/B2. Multiplication and division are done before addition.
For G, divide the freight per pair by the loaded cost already in F2: =D2/B2/F2. Excel works left to right through / and *, so you do not need brackets here.
